title: Unified usage export governance and prioritization framework for Console reporting requests
creator: Asha Patel
body:
Summary:
This ticket defines a repeatable intake, triage, and prioritization framework for customer requests related to Console reporting and usage exports. Recent enterprise customers have requested different export shapes (per-tenant cost breakdowns, model-level usage CSVs, scheduled S3 exports, and higher-fidelity per-request metadata). We need a governance rubric and an MVP scope for exports so engineering investment is predictable and aligned with enterprise needs and SLAs.

Background and motivation:
- Multiple enterprise customers (sales pipeline) requested scheduled and on-demand exports for billing reconciliation and internal chargeback.
- Current Console export flows are ad-hoc and engineering triage lacks consistent criteria for urgency and scope.
- Misaligned work has led to duplicate engineering design, unclear security controls, and missed release windows.

Goals:
1) Create a standardized intake form and scoring rubric for Console/reporting export requests.
2) Define an MVP export surface (formats, retention, fields) that satisfies 80% of incoming enterprise asks.
3) Identify security and compliance gates required for exports (PII filtering, KMS, audit logs).
4) Produce prioritization guidance for PM/ENG/Sales on when to treat a request as P0/P1/P2.

Proposed intake form (fields to capture):
- Customer org and contact, ARR or contract reference
- Use case (billing reconciliation, analytics, regulatory audit)
- Desired cadence (one-off, daily, hourly, streaming)
- Output format(s) requested (CSV, Parquet, JSONL)
- Required fields (model, route, token counts, latency, request metadata)
- Time window and retention needs
- Destination (S3/GCS/SFTP) and network restrictions (VPC, private endpoints)
- Security constraints (PII, encryption at rest, approved KMS)
- Acceptance criteria and success signal (sample reconciliation that must match)

Triage / prioritization rubric (scoring):
- Customer strategic value: 0-5 (enterprise ARR, proof-of-concept to renewal)
- Security/regulatory need: 0-5 (required for compliance)
- Engineering complexity: 0-5 (API + UI vs custom pipeline + infra) negative weight
- Reusability across customers: 0-5 (reduction in duplicated engineering)
- Time sensitivity / go-live date: 0-3 (hard deadline or flexible)

Priority mapping example:
- Score >= 12 => P0 (sales-led, security required, or renewals at risk)
- Score 8-11 => P1 (valuable and reusable, schedule in next cycle)
- Score 4-7 => P2 (batched backlog, product-led)

MVP scope (Console 1.0 exports):
- Scheduled export job: daily CSV and Parquet option for a tenant across a date range with model/route-level breakdown columns (date, model, route, tokens_in, tokens_out, latency_ms, cost_estimate).
- On-demand export API: tenant-scoped export trigger that produces a signed S3 URL for download.
- Basic filters: date range, model(s), route(s), and top-level metadata tags.
- Security: export jobs must support customer-managed KMS keys for S3 destination and generate an audit entry with operator and timestamp.
- UX: Console page to configure scheduled exports and an admin panel to view recent export jobs and statuses.

Out-of-scope for MVP (deferred):
- Per-request verbose payloads with prompt text (PII concerns) unless customer signs a data waiver.
- Streaming real-time exports (considered for a future phase).
- Highly custom aggregation pipelines per customer (may be handled as Professional Services).

Acceptance criteria (for release):
- PM-run validation with 3 pilot customers where exported CSVs match expected chargeback reports (signed off by customer finance contact).
- Security review completed and KMS integration validated against two cloud providers.
- Console UI screens implemented with scheduling, status, and download link flows.
- API surface documented and covered by integration tests; export job metrics available in observability dashboards.

Stakeholders and reviewers:
- PM lead: Asha Patel (owner)
- Eng owners: Miguel Torres (backend), Priya Singh (infra)
- Design: Leo Chen (Console UX)
- Security/compliance: Maya Reynolds
- Solutions/Sales: Carmen Ruiz (enterprise AE)

Open questions / trade-offs:
- Allowing prompt text in exports provides full fidelity for analytics but introduces high PII risk and legal overhead. Recommend default omit and add opt-in via contract.
- Storage format: Parquet reduces downstream processing costs but increases implementation time. MVP supports CSV + optional Parquet later.
- Retention policy for exports and audit logs (30 days default, extendable per contract).

Next steps / proposed timeline:
- 2026-02-25: Finalize intake form and publish in Zendesk/Salesplaybook (owner: Asha).
- 2026-03-04: Run scoring on 6 queued customer requests and present prioritization recommendations to EM forum (owner: Miguel).
- 2026-03-10: Design handoff and API contract draft (owner: Leo + Miguel).
- 2026-03-24: Engineering implementation kickoff for MVP exports (target release console-2026.04).
